documentation.range: This species is endemic to Madagascar where it is widespread across the south and southwest of the island over an area of around 125,900 km², ranging from Soalala in the west to Tranomaro  in the southeast (C. Raxworthy pers. comm. January 2011). It has been recorded between 70 and 240 m asl.
documentation.population: This is a common species. It is believed to have a stable population.
documentation.habitats: This primarily terrestrial gecko occurs in spiny scrub vegetation, where it can be found in leaf litter or on sand.
documentation.threats: There appear to be no significant threats to this species.
documentation.measures: This is a widespread species in southwestern Madagascar that is well represented in the region's protected areas. It is not listed under CITES and there is no export quota (C. Raxworthy pers. comm. June 2011).
documentation.use_trade: This species is in the international pet trade. It is unknown whether this increasingly popular gecko is yet widely bred in captivity.
documentation.rationale: Listed as Least Concern in view of its wide distribution and the absence of major threats, and because the population is unlikely to be declining
